topic: Meta publishes 'superintelligence for everyone' manifesto the same day it buries a compute auction in the fine print — the open-weights run on a single 4090, but 'free AI' still costs whatever you win the bid for (The Atlantic caught it)
prompt: an ornate golden gift box with a luxurious satin bow, half-open on a dark polished surface, inside reveals a wooden auction gavel resting on rich red velvet, dramatic single key light from the side, deep cinematic shadows, moody editorial product photography, hyper-realistic still life, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, no text, no words, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks
concept_rationale: The tweet is a bait-and-switch: 'superintelligence for everyone' (the gift) hides a compute auction (the gavel). One image, one visual paradox: an ornate golden gift box with a luxurious satin bow, half-open, revealing a wooden auction gavel resting on red velvet inside. The box is the manifesto — gilded, opulent, built to make you reach. The gavel is the auction clause — the thing that actually decides who gets the compute. Chiaroscuro key light + 85mm shallow DOF + dark polished surface keeps the visual scroll-stopping on Twitter (16:9, bold mood). Deliberately no screen, no paper, no fine-print, no Meta logo — the contradiction is structural, not literal, and rendering any of those literally would either be text (forbidden) or a brand mark (forbidden). The metaphor holds: the gift is real, and so is the gavel, and the second is what determines the first.
alt_text: An ornate golden gift box with a luxurious satin bow sits half-open on a dark polished surface, revealing a wooden auction gavel resting on rich red velvet inside, lit by a single dramatic side key light.
